messages:
samir: Customer reports their monthly credits hit 0 several hours before their local midnight (PST). They saw UI drop to 0 at ~2026-03-01 16:30 UTC and then refill at 2026-03-02 00:05 PST. They’re seeing 429s for long-running websocket streams.

jordan: Can you paste the tenant id and a quick repro? sounds like timezone/refill mismatch + caching.

samir: Tenant: acct-acme-42. Repro steps from customer: 1) start a long streaming chat session at 23:45 PST 2) keep streaming for >20 minutes 3) at local midnight the UI shows 0 tokens and new requests get 429 despite backend refill happening later. They attached a screenshot and an API curl that returns 429: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_ACME...\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{\"input\": \"ping\"}'`

maya: billing-bot, can you show the refill schedule/logs for acct-acme-42 around that window?

billing-bot: refill_job for acct-acme-42 scheduled at 00:00 UTC daily. Last run: 2026-03-02T00:00:12Z -> refill applied in DB (credits +10000) tx_id=rb-20260302-0091. Cache invalidation event queued.

jordan: Hmm DB was updated at 00:00:12Z but customer saw refill at 00:05 PST (08:05 UTC?). That gap smells like UI cache TTL or pubsub delivery delay. What are our cache TTLs for credit lookups?

maya: Current Redis key `credits:acct-acme-42` TTL = 300s (5m) per recent deploy. Refill event should `DEL` the key but we have had a race where refill writes DB then enqueues pubsub and the worker sometimes fails to DEL on first attempt. If their UI read hits the stale key before worker runs, UI shows 0. Streaming socket code reads token usage from in-memory/redis and rejects if tokens==0 -> 429.

samir: Repro idea: emulate a tenant with zero credits, start a websocket stream, then trigger refill job and see whether stream continues or gets a 429 mid-session. Who can run a quick replay?

jordan: I can run in staging. Repro steps I’ll use: 1) set redis `credits:acct-acme-42` = 0 2) open websocket and send a long request 3) trigger `refill_worker --tenant acct-acme-42 --now` 4) tail `refill_worker.log` + `pubsub-worker.log` + app logs. Will paste results.

jordan: (results) refill_worker wrote DB at 2026-03-02T00:00:12Z, pubsub queued id=pub-891, pubsub-worker tried to publish but saw transient connection error, retried, succeeded at 00:01:05Z. In that window the websocket backend read stale redis key (0) and returned a 429 for any new token allocations. After publish succeeded, app invalidated cache and new requests worked. So repro confirmed flaky pubsub path + 5m TTL causes visible window where UI and API disagree.

maya: Thanks. Root causes: a) refill applied in DB promptly b) pubsub delivery can be delayed or transient-fail c) our cache TTL+missing strict invalidation allows stale 0 to be read.

samir: Short-term mitigation for customer: flush redis key for acct-acme-42 and ask them to reconnect streams. Could we run a one-off cache flush now?

jordan: I ran: `redis-cli DEL credits:acct-acme-42` on prod shard-7 -> key removed. I also bumped their refill retry window in the worker to force immediate re-publish. Customer said they reconnected and 429s stopped.

maya: Medium-term fixes: 1) make refill worker synchronous invalidate: after DB write, attempt DEL + verify key missing; if pubsub publish fails, retry aggressively before returning success. 2) lower TTL for credits keys to 30s for tenants with streaming-enabled flag. 3) emit websocket push to active sessions on refill (we already have websocket control channel, wire this).

samir: Can product/infra prioritize (1) and (3) for SLA customers? This is an enterprise account.

maya: Filed INF-782: \"make refill atomic with cache invalidation + ws push\". Also filed SPT-441 for a customer-facing KB article: \"Why my credits showed 0 before local midnight\".

jordan: Notes for KB: explain UTC refill boundary vs local midnight, streaming session semantics (reads cache + local reservation), and recommended customer steps: reconnect after refill, call `GET /v1/billing/credits?force_refresh=true` to bypass cache, or use `billing-webhook` to monitor refill events. Example curl to force refresh: ```curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_ACME...\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/billing/credits?tenant=acct-acme-42&force_refresh=true\"```

samir: Customer updated: we flushed their cache and asked to reconnect. They confirmed services restored. They asked for why refill applies at 00:00 UTC not local midnight — we explained boundaries and linked KB draft. :thumbsup:

maya: I'll schedule a short postmortem and include repro logs + timeline. Also adding a test in integration suite that simulates transient pubsub failure during refill.

jordan: Closing loop: INF-782 assigned to infra team, ETA 2 weeks; temporary mitigation (redis DEL) is available to support ops.

samir: Thanks all — marking as resolved with follow-ups.
